title: finding(fields): FieldEditWidget declares the whole DOM pass-through block but forwards only `autoFocus` — a host's `onBlur` / `onFocus` / `id` / `name` / `tabIndex` silently never reach the control
body:
Found while measuring objectui#6859. Filed rather than folded in: it is a different
defect class from that card (which is about the data table's commit path), and it sits
one layer ABOVE the widgets rather than in them.

## What

`packages/fields/src/FieldEditWidget.tsx` declares its props as
`FieldWidgetComponentProps` (generic over any). That type is the controlled-input keys
intersected with `FieldWidgetDomProps`, `AriaAttributes`, and an open `data-` family, so
a caller may pass `id`, `name`, `autoFocus`, `tabIndex`, `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onClick`,
any `aria-` and any `data-` attribute with no type error at all.

The component body then destructures `{ field, value, onChange, readonly, autoFocus }`
and renders the resolved widget with exactly those five plus `compact`. **Everything
else is silently dropped.** Only `autoFocus` survives out of the whole DOM pass-through
block, and its doc comment explains why it in particular was forwarded — which reads
like an incomplete pass-through rather than a designed narrowing.

## Why this is the repo's own first-class class

This is the `@object-ui/fields` DECLARED-BUT-NOT-DELIVERED shape, named as first-class
in `packages/fields/src/widgets/toDomProps.ts` — "a key that type-checks, reads as
supported, and silently never reaches the element" (objectui#3290's `aria-required`,
objectui#3222's validation slot). The compile-time assertions in that file bind the
widget contract to the whitelist in both directions. Nothing binds THIS factory to
either.

## The measurement that makes it concrete

Counted over `EDIT_WIDGETS` for objectui#6859: all 27 components the map resolves to
already deliver the host's DOM set to a real control — 26 call `toDomProps` themselves,
`UserField` delegates its whole props object to `LookupField`. None of them strips
`onBlur`.

So the widgets are not the gap; this factory is. Concretely: the data table's
`renderCellEditor` seam could never hand an injected cell editor an `onBlur`, however
willing the widget, because a host handler cannot get past this destructure.

Hosts to weigh before grading: `ObjectGrid.renderCellEditor` (`packages/plugin-grid`),
`InlineFieldInput` (`packages/plugin-detail`), `RequiredFieldsDialog`
(`packages/plugin-kanban`). Whether any passes one of these keys today is the triage
question; the compiler currently says all of them may.

## Directions (not a proposal to widen anything)

1. Forward the declared block — declared = enforced, the direction `toDomProps` itself
   takes. The widgets already whitelist what may reach the DOM, so the factory would be
   passing through, not reopening a spread.
2. Or narrow this component's declared prop type to the five keys it actually honours,
   so passing the others becomes a compile error instead of a silent drop.

Either closes it; the first matches how the rest of the package resolved the same
question. Unassigned and ungraded on purpose — filed by the objectui#6859 seat.
